references.text: Describes the original instruction to take a handful of fine flour and oil from the grain offering, along with all the incense, and burn it on the altar as a memorial portion for the Lord.
The priest shall take the memorial portion from the grain offering and burn it on the altar as a fire offering, a pleasing aroma to the Lord.
The priest shall burn the memorial portion of the grain and oil, together with all the incense, as a fire offering for the Lord.
Mentions that the priest is to take a handful as a memorial portion and burn it on the altar along with the Lord's fire offerings.
Describes the burnt offering as a pleasing aroma to the Lord, a fire offering for the Lord - using the same terminology for 'ריח ניחח' (pleasing aroma).
The priest shall burn the memorial portion on the altar, following the procedure described in Leviticus 6:8.
Incense is placed on the bread rows as a memorial portion (אַזְכָּרָה), a fire offering for the Lord.
Christ gave himself for us as a gift and a sacrifice, a pleasing aroma to God - fulfilling the Old Testament sacrificial pleasing aroma.
